messages:
Miguel: Heads-up — we started seeing a steady stream of GPU preempt evictions in ap-southeast1 this morning, looks correlated with the cross-AZ compaction job that ran at 02:00 UTC. Evictions are clustered around model-serving pods that request nvlink affinity.

Miguel: snippet from kubelet/events: `Preempted: pod (gpu-model) evicted due to node packing; requested topologyAffinity: nvlink, node has mismatched nvlink pairs`

Anya: Which pools are hitting it? Hosted or Dedicated?

Miguel: Dedicated pools in ap-southeast1-a/b. Also a few Hosted jobs spilled when the compacter moved warm nodes.

Samir: We rolled the scheduler rackWeight change last night to prefer denser AZ packing. Could be interaction where compacter is consolidating across AZs and the nvlink affinity constraints then cause local evictions.

Jiayi: Can you paste the compacter job config? maybe the `spread_threshold` got tuned down.

Miguel: Config excerpt: ```yaml
# compactor config
mode: aggressive
spread_threshold: 0.05
allow_cross_az: true
prefer_nvlink_packed: false
```

Anya: prefer_nvlink_packed: false seems suspicious. That used to be true for Dedicated model pools. If compacter doesn't preserve NVLink topology, we get packing that breaks pod affinity.

Ops-Lead: We saw a small spike in GPU unit-cost yesterday too — cross-AZ egress bumped when pods moved. cc @finance for cost note. :money_with_wings:

Samir: Ok re-opening the scheduler rollout (revert rackWeight) might reduce compaction pressure. But we should also make compacter topology-aware.

Jiayi: Metric to watch: `scheduler.topology_mismatch_evictions` and `compactor.cross_az_moves`. Miguel, can you link dashboards?

Miguel: Dashboard links: https://grafana/redwood/d/compaction and https://grafana/redwood/d/scheduler-topology. Current graph shows compactor moves spike at 02:03 and evictions spike at 02:11.

Anya: Immediate mitigation: throttle compactor to `mode: conservative` and set `prefer_nvlink_packed: true`. That should avoid moving nvlink-dependent pods. Can someone do a quick canary?

Ops-Lead: I'll flip the compactor to conservative for ap-southeast1 as a canary. Deploy-Bot: please run the change with 10m pause window.

Deploy-Bot: deploy job started by Ops-Lead: compactor-mode-toggle -> canary(ap-southeast1) -> pause=10m. Logs: deploy accepted. :white_check_mark:

Samir: Parallel step: I'll start rollback of the rackWeight change in the scheduler for ap-southeast1. If compactor is topology-aware and scheduler weight is reverted, we should stop the eviction loop.

Jiayi: Long-term: compactor needs a topology policy that preserves NVLink/GPU bonding. Add tests to the scheduler simulator that model nvlink-aware packing. I'll own the design doc.

Miguel: After canary flip: evictions dropped 70% in the first 15m. Cross-AZ egress also trending down.

Anya: Great. Action items: 1) Ops-Lead: keep compactor conservative for 24h in ap-southeast1. 2) Samir: rollback rackWeight in scheduler for the same region. 3) Jiayi: design doc + simulator tests for nvlink topology by end of sprint. 4) Miguel: surface affected customer manifests to CS.

Ops-Lead: noted and doing 1) now. Will update runbook entry: https://runbook.redwood/compactor-topology-issues.

Miguel: tagging @Anya @Samir @Jiayi for follow-ups. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Anya: If anyone sees any residual pod flapping, drop it here.

Samir: I'll monitor `scheduler.topology_mismatch_evictions` and post alerts if it rises above baseline.

Deploy-Bot: canary complete, no failures reported.

Miguel: closing thread unless new flaps show up.
